- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, increase forecast slightly to reflect bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast to avoid overcorrection or overshoot.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model tends to overreact — cap forecast growth to 5–7% per period to avoid overshoot.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling after peak), model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast slope in such periods.  
- If history shows recent volatility or sentiment swings, model overfits to recent trend — use 3–5 day smoothing or lagged average to dampen noise.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently below true outcome by >5% over 3–5 days, adjust upward by 1–2% per day to account for lagged sentiment effects.
